chunks: And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said:

"Allah, Glorious is His Majesty, said: 'Whichever servant obeys Me, I do not entrust him to other than Me; and whichever servant disobeys Me, I leave him to himself, then I do not care in which valley he perishes.'"

key_terms.أَطَاعَنِي: obeys Me; fulfills obedience to Allah
key_terms.أَكِلْهُ إِلَى غَيْرِي: I entrust him to other than Me; I leave him under another's charge
key_terms.عَبْدٍ: servant; the human being in relation to Allah
key_terms.عَصَانِي: disobeys Me; acts in defiance of Allah
key_terms.فِي أَيِّ وَادٍ هَلَكَ: in whichever valley he perishes; a metaphor for destruction without divine care
key_terms.وَكَلْتُهُ إِلَى نَفْسِهِ: I leave him to himself; I abandon him to his own soul and capacity

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about obeying Allah and being left to one's own self?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that obedience to Allah brings divine care and protection, while disobedience results in a person being left to his own self. It emphasizes the theological and ethical danger of self-reliance apart from Allah and the safety found in submission to Him.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5869 - Messenger of Allah (swt), peace and blessings be upon him and his family, said:

"Allah (swt), the Glorified and Exalted, said:
'Whoever of My (swt) servants obeys Me (swt), I will not entrust him to anyone other than Myself (swt). And whoever disobeys Me (swt), I will leave him to himself, and I will not care in which valley he perishes.'"
